we introduce a model that can reconstruct multiple people in the same image and we show how to do it in a physically plausible and consistent manner, using only monocular images and without any 3D supervision.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of transformer-based architectures with mesh-based collision detection can be a promising approach for the challenging 3D reconstruction of multiple people in close proximity.

the combination of self- and interaction-contact losses with a transformer network allows us to learn a model that can reconstruct multiple people from a single image, even when the number and pose of people is not known a-priori, while being robust to self- and inter-person occlusion.
